winning_patterns: Short 13-15 second clips with high-energy crash or physics break hooks outperformed 30-second medium clips by nearly 2x median views (531 vs 271).
Clips featuring streamer names in the hook combined with a specific game failure (crashing, physics broke, painting wrong) drove the highest cross-platform views.
YouTube Shorts dominated total volume with 10,405 views, while TikTok delivered higher engagement rates per view for mid-tier streamer clips.
avoid_patterns: Reject 30-second generic street gameplay or beach truck chaos clips with no streamer reaction or game-breaking moment.
Reject clips with zero likes, shares, or comments across all platforms, such as Jason the Ween and Kai Cenat flops.
Reject hooks that lack urgency or specific streamer attribution, resulting in 1-2 view dead posts.
hook_style_guidance: Write Frame-1 hooks that combine a streamer name, a specific GTA 6 failure or chaos moment, and all-caps urgency to stop the scroll immediately.
daily_brief: The biggest win was the ohnepixel crash clip hitting 10,910 views with a 13-second hook, while the biggest leak is 30-second generic gameplay clips getting 1-86 views. Tomorrow, cut all clips to 15 seconds max and only publish streamer reaction moments with game-breaking physics or crashes.
